title: "Transformer"
description: "A neural-network architecture built around attention and feed-forward layers for processing sequences and other structured inputs."
term: "Transformer"
letter: "T"
category: "Deep Learning"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

A Transformer processes input representations using attention, which lets
parts of the input exchange information. Transformers power many language,
vision, and multimodal models.

## Technical explanation

Transformer layers commonly combine multi-head attention, feed-forward
networks, residual connections, and normalization. Encoder, decoder, and
encoder-decoder variants use different attention masks and information
flows. Positional information is needed to represent order.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Transformers underpin many foundation models and provide a flexible
architecture for sequence and multimodal tasks. Their compute and memory
requirements, context handling, and inference behavior influence system
design.

## How it works

Inputs are embedded and supplied with positional information. Attention
forms context-aware representations, and feed-forward sublayers transform
them. Stacking layers builds richer representations. Decoder-only language
models use causal masks so each position predicts from permitted preceding
context.

## Practical example

A decoder-only Transformer can receive token IDs and predict a probability
distribution for the next token. At generation time, the application
repeatedly samples or selects a token and appends it to the context.

## Common misconceptions

- A Transformer is an architecture family, not a single model or training
  objective.
- Attention alone does not encode order; architectures add positional
  signals or related mechanisms.
